record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: Can a peer-to-peer data-sharing system provide meaningful anonymity guarantees while also maintaining efficiency, decentralization, and the ability of peers to discover one another and locate content?

evidence.quote: We would ideally like to provide anonymity while maintaining other desirable search and security features such as efficiency, decentralization, and peer discovery.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a peer-to-peer data-sharing system modeled as a dynamic distributed network in which a set of autonomous peers store data objects and respond to queries from other peers. Each peer may act as a publisher, a requester, or a forwarder. Define the following desiderata for such a system:

(1) Anonymity: there exists a precise indistinguishability-style guarantee (for example, publisher anonymity, requester anonymity, and/or unlinkability between requesters and the content they retrieve) that holds against a global passive adversary, or at least against an adversary that controls a constant fraction of peers and observes all network traffic adjacent to those peers.

(2) Efficiency: queries are resolved using poly-logarithmic (in the number of peers and objects) communication, latency, and per-peer storage and bandwidth overhead.

(3) Decentralization: no peer or fixed set of peers is required to participate in every query or to hold global state; all operations are symmetric across peers up to local resources.

(4) Peer discovery and content location: any peer can, starting from limited local knowledge, discover other participating peers and successfully locate any content that is published in the system, with high probability.

Question: Does there exist a protocol for such a peer-to-peer data-sharing system that simultaneously satisfies properties (1), (2), (3), and (4), or is there an inherent trade-off (provable lower bound) showing that some pair among anonymity, efficiency, decentralization, and discoverability cannot be jointly achieved?
artifact.status_search_result: Combining strong anonymity with efficiency, decentralization, and peer/content discovery in P2P systems remains an active open research challenge. Anonymous P2P designs (Freenet, Tarzan, Tor-based overlays, Dissent, Riposte, etc.) continue to trade off latency, scalability, or anonymity strength, and no protocol is known to simultaneously achieve all four properties with provable guarantees, nor has a definitive impossibility result been established.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Anonymous Communication Systems with a Focus on P2P
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys note that achieving strong anonymity together with low-latency, scalable, decentralized content discovery remains an unsolved design problem in P2P networks.
status_evidence.claim: No anonymous P2P system to date achieves strong anonymity together with efficiency, decentralization, and effective content/peer discovery.
